title: Declarative output contracts and graceful tool-degradation acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: Customers are integrating Redwood with multi-step toolchains (search, DB upsert, external API calls). We need a clear, testable spec for 'declarative output contracts' — a minimal, explicit schema wrapper that the LLM can emit during streaming or non-streaming runs to indicate structured payloads, tool invocation intents, and finalization semantics. This ticket captures acceptance criteria, observability signals, error modes, and an operator fallback playbook for cases where downstream tool invocation is degraded. Goals: Provide a deterministic contract that lets SDKs and proxies: 1) reliably detect tool call boundaries during partial streams, 2) validate final schema and surface repairable vs unrecoverable errors, 3) fall back to a best-effort text mode when structured output cannot be guaranteed, and 4) provide signals to console and customer's telemetry for incident classification. Scope clarifications: This PRD focuses on the spec and acceptance tests for the output contract and tool-fallback behavior. Implementation details for runtime kernel selection, batching, or SMT quantization are OOB. Work includes spec doc, unit/integration tests against the Hosted API, SDK parsing behavior (JS/Python), and Console telemetry dashboards. Non-goals: Changing function-calling invocation semantics (auth, parameter mapping) and internal runtime retries for tool gateway are separate tickets. Key definitions (for reviewers): - Declarative contract: a small JSON-like frame emitted by the model with predictable start/end markers and a versioned schema stamp (e.g., contract_v1). - Finality marker: an explicit token that indicates the model has completed emitting structured output for this request. - Repairable error: syntactic or partial-schema violations that the server/SDK can attempt to auto-correct (e.g., missing optional field, truncated array) and rehydrate a best-effort call payload. - Unrecoverable error: semantic mismatch or missing required fields that must surface as a client-facing failure. Deliverables: - Spec doc (Confluence): "Declarative Output Contract v1" describing frame layout, versioning, and error classes. - SDK parsing tests (JS + Python) demonstrating correct detection and fallback. - Acceptance test harness: synthetic streaming tests covering normal, truncated, and interleaved non-structured tokens. - Console dashboard panel: counts of detected contract failures, repair attempts, and tool-call success/failure split. Why this matters: Customers building critical flows (in-product actions, payments, data writes) require deterministic guarantees that structured tool calls will occur only when schema is satisfied. This reduces silent data corruption and enables automated rollbacks and compensating transactions in downstream services.
acceptance_checklist: Contract frame detected: SDKs must detect a contract frame start and end in >= 99% of successful synthetic streams (test harness).
Versioning: contract_v1 stamp present in all emitted frames for rollout compatibility.
Finality marker: finality token must be emitted within the same stream and be unambiguous.
Repair policy: SDK repair attempts count must be logged and repair success rate >= 95% for repairable error fixtures.
Fallback: when unrecoverable, the request must fall back to unstructured_text mode and return a clear error code to client.
Observability: Console must surface contract_finality distribution and link to failed traces in the runtime tracer.
test_plan: Unit: validate SDK parser accepts canonical contract frames and rejects malformed frames (JS + Python).
Streaming integration: simulate partial network truncation (mid-frame) and assert server marks as 'truncated_contract' and SDK either attempts repair or surfaces an error according to policy.
Tool-call dry-run: when contract is valid, server should emit a tool_call event to the middleware layer with a call_id; validate idempotency by replaying duplicate call_id.

Fallback behavior: when contract validation fails with repairable errors, SDK should attempt canonical repairs (fill defaults, close unclosed arrays) and proceed to tool-call within 2s; if unsuccessful, fallback to 'unstructured_text' mode and record event.
Chaos test: interleave benign natural-language tokens between contract frames and validate parser resilience.
Backpressure test: under high concurrency ensure contract detection latency stays < 50ms p95 in SDK parsing path.
telemetry_requirements: Emit 'contract_detected' boolean per request with contract_version label.
Emit 'contract_finality' enum: success | truncated | malformed | repaired | unrecoverable.
Emit 'tool_call' event with labels: call_id, tool_name, attempt_count, result (success | failure | blocked).
Record time-to-first-contract-frame (ms) and time-to-finality (ms) for latency SLO analysis.
Expose repair_attempts and repaired_success counters to Console for per-tenant breakdown.
Tag telemetry with deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private for correlation.
operator_playbook: If > 5% of requests in a 1h window are 'unrecoverable', set incident channel and tag runtime team.
For rising 'repaired' rates, toggle 'strict_contract_enforcement' at runtime (console switch) to force explicit failure for debugging.
When a tool gateway reports >= 10% 5xxs for calls originating from contract frames, automatically enable 'degrade_to_text' routing for that tool and notify solutions engineering.
Dedicated customers: on large-scale contract failures, contact CSM, enable tenant-scoped circuit-breaker, and schedule a tenant remediation runbook.
